what: LM-PAIRED (2026-10-17): the blueprint's paired comparison (BCIR_Training_Architecture_Blueprint_2026-10-13, sections 5 and 11) -- BCIR against the fastest matched PyTorch configuration on this host, torch.compile with fused AdamW, seed by seed: the 1,000-step language-model run at four threads, BCIR under kblock+exp+reduce, five seeds (the 10-11 record's 20261011 and 1001, 2002, 3003, 4004: each seed its own initial weights and batch schedule, the corpus, its splits and the held-out problems the same), one pair a seed in one session, the pair's order alternating seed by seed. The analysis was fixed before the runs (paired.py's docstring): the speed ratio of the two median warm steps per seed, their geometric mean with a 95% Student-t interval over the seeds' log ratios; the quality margin, the 95% interval of BCIR's test cross-entropy minus PyTorch's inside +-0.01 nats.
host: 4-vCPU Intel Xeon @ 2.10GHz container (family 6 model 207; AVX-512 with AVX512-BF16/FP16 and AMX, which neither side uses here; 48 KB L1d and 2 MB L2 a core, a 260 MB L3) -- ../pack/'s instance, not ../lm/'s r9 one (2.80 GHz, 1 MB L2, 33 MB L3) -- GCC 13.3 (the trainer builds), PyTorch 2.13.0 at four intra-op threads, Python 3.11.15 (the declared floor); every run FP32; indicative wall times, no PMU

files.run.sh: the rounds as run (bash run.sh OUT TORCH_PYTHON from the repository root: prepare per seed, then the pairs), on aeb7d15 (train_comparison.py's prepare --seed and the train records' memory split; runtime/c is d68e3d3's)
files.paired.py, summary.json: the analysis fixed before the runs, with the check added after them (labelled so in its docstring and output), and its output over runs/
files.runs/{bcir,torch-compiled}-<seed>.json: the ten train records (train_comparison.py's train stage): losses, gradient norms, every step's seconds, the evaluations, the final validation and test metrics, the state digest, peak RSS and the memory split
files.eager.sh, runs/torch-eager-{20261011,100: the check added after the runs: eager PyTorch (torch.optim.AdamW defaults) on two of the seeds in the same session, after the pairs

reading: Speed: seed 1001 177.1 / 226.1 ms (1.277); seed 2002 177.1 / 222.9 ms (1.258); seed 3003 176.5 / 218.4 ms (1.237); seed 4004 177.8 / 223.5 ms (1.257); seed 20261011 185.2 / 237.4 ms (1.282). The geometric mean ratio 1.262, 95% interval 1.240-1.284; BCIR faster on 5 of 5 seeds. Quality: BCIR's test cross-entropy minus PyTorch's -0.00001 nats on average, 95% interval -0.00006 to +0.00003 (inside the +-0.01 margin); validation +0.00011. Memory: peak RSS 528-529 MB against 1055-1121; the persistent state 157,390,848 bytes on both (weights, gradients and both moments), BCIR's transient arena 194,019,328 bytes (PyTorch's transient activations have no peak counter on CPU), torch.compile's compile and first two steps 5.7-31.6 s outside its median. Check added after the runs: eager PyTorch on seeds 20261011 and 1001 took 235.5 and 254.6 ms a step (0.8% faster and 12.6% slower than that seed's compiled run; 20261011's compiled run was the session's first, its compile 31.6 s), so against the faster PyTorch arm wherever both ran the ratio is 1.260 (95% interval 1.241-1.279).
